function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I don’t have real‑time access to a live calendar, so I can’t tell you *exactly* which event will be the very next thing happening in the U.S. at this moment. However, based on the most recent schedules that were publicly available as of my last update, the next major festival that’s slated to take place in the United States is **South by Southwest (SXSW)** in Austin, Texas.

---

## South by Southwest (SXSW) – 2026 Edition  
**Dates:** March 11–20, 2026  
**Location:** Austin Convention Center, Auditorium Theatre, and various venues around downtown Austin, TX  
**Website:** [https://www.sxsw.com](https://www.sxsw.com)

### What It Is
SXSW is a multi‑disciplinary festival that brings together music, film, and interactive media. It’s known for:

| Category | Highlights |
|----------|------------|
| **Music** | 200+ stages, 1,500+ artists, spanning indie rock, hip‑hop, electronic, world music, and more |
| **Film** | 400+ screenings, 100+ premieres, 30+ awards |
| **Interactive** | 300+ exhibitors, 70+ conferences, 20+ hackathons |
| **Networking** | 10,000+ attendees, 2,000+ industry professionals |

### Ticketing (as of the latest public info)
| Ticket Type | Price (USD) | Notes |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| Early Bird (pre‑sale) | $199 | Limited availability, sold out quickly |
| General Admission | $249 | Includes access to all music stages, film screenings, and interactive events |
| VIP | $499 | Includes backstage passes, meet‑and‑greet opportunities, and premium seating |

> **Tip:** Tickets often sell out within hours of release. Keep an eye on the official SXSW site and sign up for their newsletter to get alerts on ticket drops.

### Travel & Accommodation
- **Flights:** Austin–Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) is the main gateway. Book early for the best rates.
- **Hotels:** The city offers a range of options from boutique hotels to budget hostels. Many hotels offer “SXSW packages” that bundle lodging with festival passes.
- **Transportation:** Austin’s public transit (Capital Metro) runs frequent buses and a light rail system. Ride‑share services (Uber/Lyft) are widely available.

### Why It Might Be the Next Big Thing
- **Timing:** SXSW typically kicks off in early March, which is usually the first major festival window after the winter holidays.
- **Scale:** With thousands of attendees and a global media presence, it’s a prime spot for networking, brand exposure, and cultural immersion.
- **Diversity:** The festival’s blend of music, film, and tech makes it appealing to a wide audience—from creatives to entrepreneurs.

---

## Quick Checklist Before You Go

| Item | Action |
|------|--------|
| **Tickets** | Purchase as soon as they’re available; consider a package that includes lodging. |
| **Accommodation** | Book a hotel or Airbnb near downtown Austin; many offer early‑bird discounts. |
| **Travel** | Book flights early; consider flexible dates if you’re traveling from outside Texas. |
| **Packing** | Bring comfortable shoes, a reusable water bottle, a portable charger, and a small backpack for day‑to‑day essentials. |
| **Health & Safety** | Check the festival’s COVID‑19 policy (if applicable) and bring any required masks or proof of vaccination. |
| **Schedule** | Download the official SXSW app or print a schedule to plan your days. |

---

### Bottom Line
If you’re looking for the next big festival in the U.S., SXSW 2026 is the most imminent major event on the calendar. It’s a great opportunity to experience cutting‑edge music, film, and tech, and to network with industry professionals. Just remember that festival schedules can shift, so double‑check the official SXSW website or reputable ticket vendors for the most up‑to‑date information.

Enjoy the festival season!
